title: Algolia requires invalid router in next js 13 app directory
body:
### 🐛 Current behavior

The latest version of next.js 13 and algolia react-instantsearch-hooks-router-nextjs is incompatible because it requires that you import a router that only works with the old pages directory. To my understanding, nextjs uses { useRouter } from "next/navigation" when you need a router in a client component. Can you please recommend a fix to this issue? I would really appreciate any help.

"use client";
import { SingletonRouter } from "next/router";
import { createInstantSearchRouterNext } from "react-instantsearch-hooks-router-nextjs";

<InstantSearch  indexName="products" searchClient={searchClient}  routing={{ router: createInstantSearchRouterNext({           singletonRouter })}}>

### 🔍 Steps to reproduce

1. Use the latest next.js 13
2. Add reactinstantsearch-hooks-router-nextjs
3. Try to use this on a "use client" page or normal "server" page in the new "app" directory.
4. You'll get an error saying that next/router can't be used on anything other than a client page.

### Live reproduction

https://codesandbox.io

### 💭 Expected behavior

Work with { useRouter } or any other router option in the app directory of next js 13.

### Package version

react-instantsearch-hooks-router-nextjs 6.4.73

### Operating system

_No response_

_No response_

comments.body:
Hey @chrissshh,

This is because the custom router was made for the `pages` directory router.

From my experience when doing CSR with the `app` dir, simply having `<InstantSearch routing={true}>` works out of the box as Next.js no longer relies on having a specific key in history to know whether it should rerender when back/forward browser button has been pressed.

Can you please tell me what's not working with `routing={true}` ?

The reason we don't document it is that we still don't support SSR with the `app` dir, but maybe it's worth documenting that for CSR.

Is there anywhere you can find a guide on how to sync query variables with the next URL in the nextjs App router? I am unsure how to this really. I use Algolia for search functionality only inside a modal, so everything is running clientside.

Hey @LarsEjaas, as we're not currently officially supporting the app router, there is none yet.
Could you provide a CodeSandbox showcasing what are the exact problems you have so that we can provide a workaround and/or take that into account when we officially support the app router ?

Hi @aymeric-giraudet 

Thanks for taking the time to help 🙂  

I have created this sandbox:
https://codesandbox.io/p/sandbox/nice-phoebe-c5qxtt

I have the same issue with the page router in Nextjs as well as the app router. I am unsure how to sync the query variables with the URL(and still be able to navigate back and forth in the history of the Nextjs router). I want a search modal on top of the page making it possible to search all app/page content.

I am looking at this page:
https://www.algolia.com/doc/api-reference/widgets/instantsearch-next-router/react/
Here it is explicitly stated that:
`createInstantSearchNextRouter() is a function that creates a Next.js-compatible InstantSearch router to pass to InstantSearch... ...This function cannot be used in conjunction with getStaticProps. Use getServerSideProps() or client-side rendering instead.`

I have tried making a very basic codesandbox - but all the Algolia code will of course be lazy-loaded when the user opens the modal the first time. 

This functionality seemed fairly easy to do with React InstantSearch v6. But in v7 in the Nextjs app router I have a hard time figuring out how to do this.

Hey @aymeric-giraudet  do you guys have an ETA by any chance on App router support?
Is it something currently on your roadmap?
It's definitely on our roadmap and we're actively working on it (see POCs in #5828 and #5827), but we have no timeline on this as of yet.

Hey @ddaoxuan and @chrissshh !

We released an experimental package for App Router support, and it supports routing already : https://www.algolia.com/doc/guides/building-search-ui/going-further/server-side-rendering/react/#app-router-experimental
You can activate routing simply by adding a `routing` boolean prop to `InstantSearchNext`.

I'll close this as it's now solved !
